Not a great teacher:
- Handwriting is poor
- Makes mistakes sometimes when writing things
- Kinda monotone guy
- I think he gave 1 quiz in lecture that counts as participation? and then never again. I didn't go that day, so oh well.
- He didn't have any practice exams for each midterm, which I didn't like.
- The homework would deduct points for answers you got wrong, which I think is kind of harsh. Small mistakes can chip away at your homework grade.
- Quizzes in discussion were only like 5-10 minutes long, which was too little time for me to think properly sometimes.

First exam was terrible for everyone; he didn't really give us any info, and the problems weren't really like what we've learned before. I think he noticed that, because he did give everyone more info on how the next exams would go, and made it more like our homework problems, so that was nice.

Final was terrible for everyone. I hope there's a curve, but he hasn't said anything about it yet.

PHYS260 is just a hard class in general, but I think this guy increased the difficulty by a fair amount. Don't take him if you can help it.

Wendell Hill is an experienced and clearly knowledgeable physicist. Unfortunately, that knowledge does not make him a good lecturer.

Lectures feel disconnected from homework, quizzes, and exams. The board fills up with dense symbols and unclear handwriting while the monotone delivery assumes you already learned the material somewhere else. Attendance is maybe encouraged through bonus points, which is generous, because being physically present does not mean you will understand anything. Asking a question feels like volunteering to be publicly humiliated. He has a special talent for making you feel stupid for not understanding something while also not fully answering the question.

Time-consuming ExpertTA and written homework assignments, along with weekly discussion quizzes, make it clear very quickly that lecture is not meant to prepare you. To succeed, you are expected to teach yourself the entire course using the textbook, YouTube, or even by hiring a tutor. Even then, you will likely still be relying on a curve by the end of the course.

Overall, he is a prime example of why people dislike tenured professors. This class demands a high level of independence and endurance. If you have the option, take physics somewhere else.

Professor Girvan is a good professor for physics 2. She really cares and takes the time to explain each concept, walk through derivations, and work on example problems. The lectures are hard to get through, one due to the content being tough to grasp, and two because the slides are hard to follow and she goes fast. However, ample resources are provided on her ELMS page and through the textbook. She always posts practice for the exams, and use them, because the actual exams are challenging. She also does in person quizzes every week that are based off the homework. Regarding homework, there are usually two assignments a week. The hw includes an online portion through expert ta and a written portion that could either be textbook or expert ta problems. The homework goes in depth with the material which I found useful. Professor Girvan’s PHYS260 class is a lot of work and is challenging but I felt it really helped me grasp concepts and learn the material more than the students in the other phys 2 lectures. Professor Girvan is happy to answer any questions and work with you through any troubles in the course. Would recommend for this course

Very poor lecturer, teaches class over slides and writes on them but his handwriting is terrible and impossible to understand, he left multiple times over the semester for research, class was behind schedule the entire time. His tests are so weirdly difficult and unordinary, i looked at some of my friends tests who were taking other professors and they were actually understandable. the first year he comes back to teach 260 and writes a large part of the final it has a 48% average... would not recommend taking his class at all, or believing the few positive reviews lol.

Professor Girvan was a phenomenal physics 2 teacher, she’s posts two sets of every lecture slides, constantly asks for feedback in class that is immediately implemented, offers redos of your worst exam grade and explains things clearly.  The class is fast paced and there is a lot of work ( weekly quizzes and online and written homework) but it prepares you super well for the tests.  I would highly recommend taking her

In short take her for PHYS260, yes! Honestly, Dr. Girvan is rated a bit harshly. There are a lot of assignments in this class, and you will need to put in the work, however, it's all to prepare you for the midterm and the final exam. Trust me. Her lectures and slides are amazing! Her slides are top tier. Lectures are great but sometimes could go too theoretical in my opinion, but she is a physicist so that makes sense. If you want to actually learn, definitely take her. If not, there's nothing wrong with that, but she might not be the professor for you.

I am not going to lie to you—this course is extremely challenging, but Michelle is a really good teacher. She genuinely cares about whether students understand the material and takes the time to explain difficult concepts clearly. Her lectures are well organized, and she is always willing to slow down, answer questions, or revisit topics if the class is struggling.

Her exam questions are taken directly from her notes, so if you keep up with the material and study what she emphasizes in class, the exams feel fair and manageable. While the workload can be heavy and the pace demanding, you can tell that she wants students to succeed and truly learn the content rather than just memorize it. Overall, this is a tough course, but it is taught by someone who is supportive, approachable, and invested in her students’ success.

Pros: Genuinely cares about students doing well, good example problems, assigns a lot of homework (which makes you actually engage with the material)
Cons: You need stimulants to keep up with her in lecture, you have to memorize equations for quizzes (but not for exams?) and her mic is way louder than it needs to be.
Honestly don't get why her rating is lower than Hailu's, she was a decent professor for a hard class (while Hailu's lectures can lull you to sleep and his exams were apparently cruel). If you have to choose between her, Hill and Hailu, take her.

WOW his lectures will put you to sleep, for that reason alone not worth going. Otherwise exams are medium difficulty and based on homework/in class problems (he does upload his slides), so if you can self study stuff it's fine ig.
Quizzes are straightforward, but the final this year was hilariously hard for some reason (it legit looked nothing like previous years, he gave us past finals to study). Otherwise he's pretty receptive to emails and even gave us points back on exam 1 on a problem that was ambiguously worded by mistake, but overall just not great professor for this subject. Find someone else and save yourself the headache

Professor Girvan is a really good and caring professor. I personally enjoyed how much attention she pays to students and tries to help them to the best of her ability. I recommend reading the book before coming to class prepared and ready to do the practice problems she puts on the board. The class itself is very hard but the exams were graded very lightly.

Why are people hating on her. She's genuinely the best physics professor I've had in my entire life. Her exams were really fair and straightforward.  I think if you put into the effort needed, you will have a good grade.

His lectures can be helpful when he is going through examples, however that is all the lectures are. He does not really try to explain the physics, but instead just gives a formula and does the math. I used the textbook in expert ta which was helpful and also provided some good examples. His midterms were mostly fine, and doing the examples in the textbook and reviewing the homework prepared me well. Overall, you will have to teach yourself as he is mostly a non factor in your ability to succeed. The homework and quizzes provide a nice cushion and it is definitely possible to do well in the class.

I don't understand why professor Girvan has a low rating on this website. Yes the content in this class is confusing and the averages on the exams are low but she is an amazing lecturer. She is very good at answering questions during class and is great at pointing out the key parts of example problems as she goes through them. She did ok at making the lectures interesting but with them being so long its hard. Her exams are somewhat difficult but you are allowed to create your own large note sheet with whatever you want on it. She provided a strange curve at the end of the course which was: A+: ≥ 96, A: 90–95.99, A-: 86–89.99, B+: 80–85.99, B: 75–79.99, B-: 70–74.99, C+: 65–69.99, C: 60–64.99, C-: 50–59.99, D: 40–49.99, F: < 40. The discussion section had a quiz every week which the averages were either a 6 or 7 out of 10. Overall was a very poor use of discussion time and most people left right after the quiz learning nothing. Overall she is a good lecturer with tests being difficult but fair with a nice curve at the low end but discussion time being used poorly...
Save yourself time and take someone else

Absolute trash. Take heidarian. Tests are a little hard but not insane. Except for the final, the average was a 58. Grading is very harsh. Lectures are so boring you might fall asleep. If you fall asleep worry not, as the lectures are so useless for learning the content and how to actually solve problems that you will have missed nothing.
By no means is this class easy. Lectures are sometimes confusing but usually his exam material is pulled or extremely similar to homework or lecture.

I would not recommend taking Hailu for the basic fact that he is beyond lazy with the materials he provides for his students and you can basically teach yourself significantly better with the textbook in the time it takes him to work through a problem in class. If you took him for 161, imagine that class but sped up with harder content, however the textbook is fairly comprehensive and has all the examples he pulls from for the class. I will say the homework is excessively long and tedious and isn't a great teacher of the test material and concepts, so be sure to do challenge problems from the textbook before the exams, which will be make or break for your grade. This class is much more conceptual than 161 so find a good TA to help you digest content wherever possible. Only take this class if you plan to learn out of a textbook anyways, and even with that the content is tough. Good Luck

I will preface this with saying that I took Hailu the previous semester for 161, that class was easy and thought he was chill so I went with him again. Hailu's lectures are very hard to get anything out of, in the end you just learn the content through the homeworks and videos, at least that's what I did. As in 161, he again goes through derivations of equations, but they go on for so long that it's pointless and he shows you more than what you'll actually need. Just look at the equations on his slides and write that down. As usual for Hailu style, his exams are fair but do make sure to write down equations that you may think are useless as anything is "fair game".

Would give him a 0 if I could. The Wendell Hill experience guarantees:
1. He tries to solve a problem on screen, but does it incorrectly, taking away time the next lecture to correct his mistakes (which was for a problem ripped straight out of the textbook!)
2. Has to "correct" some things in his slides from when he last taught this course (10 years ago!)
3. Mumbles a lot AND refuses to use a mic (in a lecture hall!) AND has horrible handwriting. Even if you are sitting in front row, 50% of the info will not be coherent. 
4. "Walk us through derivations" by putting up symbols on the board and telling us to "turn the crank" (Thank you Professor Hill for walking us halfway through a textbook problem! PLEASE don't go through some problems similar to ones that show up on the midterms....)

Lowest midterm got dropped 
Generous curve (85+ is an A roughly)
Cool demos if the equipment works (~50% of the time)

Summary: Hill makes the class harder than it needs to be, just read the textbook and do some textbook/expert TA practice problems, ask the TAs questions during discussion.

The material in the course was hard and Hailu's lecture's weren't too bad. Yes he can put you to sleep pretty fast but if you stay awake his lectures are somewhat useful. If you do the homeworks legit and do previous exams you should be set for a decent grade. Only went to discussion to pick up my exams so don't know how much of a help the TA's were.

Lots of material for an incredibly difficult class, and I’m so happy with what she did give us. Lectures were fast paced, but the notes online were excellent to follow. The online homework was difficult but fair, and the written homework sometimes felt impossible, but that one was graded on completion so if I spent more than 3-4 hours I’d just phone it in and still get full marks. My TA was alright, but Girvain herself has wonderful resources and was amazing during office hours. It’s not a fun class, but Girvain is an excellent choice to succeed with. The curve was also pretty great, with only 5% of students failing, with her saying they were often students who didn’t try at all.

Girvan has to be the best professor rated this low at UMD. She's definitely the best option for 260 (although her competition is pretty bad). The class is hard, but that's really due to the material, not her. Her slides are pretty clear, and she does a ton of examples. She also makes sure to answer all of the questions she has time for. She is very nice and understanding, and repeatedly asked the class for feedback on certain policies (and would adapt based on our responses). Her exams are hard, but they're easier than the other two profs from Fall 2025. They're also all very similar to homework/lecture examples, plus you get an unrestricted formula sheet (so you can put examples on it). The worst thing about this class, in my opinion, is the TAs. Some of them seem to have 0 clue what's going on in the class, as they likely haven't seen this material in many years (I believe they're all post-grad students). But that doesn't affect the course much since Girvan is very available for questions, and the quizzes were all clear and not too difficult (compared to the material).
Lectures did not teach me the required materials. If you have difficulty learning on your own, do not take this professor.
